title: DiagonalSmoothStronglyConvexBlackBox.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable convex minimization on R^d, with an attained minimum.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: For W=diag(w), w_i>0, the first-order remainder lies between μ||y-x||_W²/2 and ||y-x||_W²/2; 0<μ≤1. Initially f(x0)-f*≤Δ, with Δ≥0.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query returns the exact full Euclidean gradient together with the function value, regardless of history or seed.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The exact function value is included in every full-gradient oracle reply; the pair counts as one oracle call.

distinctive_assumptions.label: unknown_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Only d and x0 are public. The positive diagonal weights w, relative strong-convexity parameter μ, initial-gap bound Δ, and target ε are hidden from the algorithm constructor.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: Smoothness and strong convexity share the unknown weighted norm ||v||_W²=Σ_i w_i v_i². The supplied budget is independent of the magnitudes and spread of the weights.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain and output space are EuclideanSpace R (Fin d), with d≥1 public.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output must satisfy f(output)-f(xstar)≤ε for a global minimizer xstar, with ε>0.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, after the supplied fixed oracle budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation hides the entire diagonal geometry and all convergence parameters while requiring a fixed-budget, almost-sure objective guarantee with weight-independent oracle complexity.

descriptionHtml:
Hidden Diagonal Curvature Minimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable function f:Rd→R, where d≥1, with a given starting point x0∈Rd. For hidden weights w1,…,wd>0, its first-order remainder lies between μ∥y−x∥w2/2 and ∥y−x∥w2/2, where ∥v∥w2=∑i=1dwivi2 and 0<μ≤1. A global minimizer x⋆ satisfies f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ, with Δ≥0. The oracle returns (f(x),∇f(x)) at x. For ε>0, the goal is f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Rdf(x). The inner product and gradient are Euclidean. The algorithm receives only d and x0; the weights w1,…,wd, relative curvature parameter μ, initial gap bound Δ, and tolerance ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Diagonal curvature bounds). The function f is differentiable everywhere. For every x,y∈Rd, f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+12∥y−x∥w2,f(y)≥f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+μ2∥y−x∥w2.

Assumption 2 (Initial objective gap). There exists x⋆∈Rd such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈Rd,f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ.

Queries may be made at any point of Rd, with each call returning the exact function value and Euclidean gradient together. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯∈Rd must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
On Rd, d≥1, differentiable f satisfies μ2∥y−x∥w2≤f(y)−f(x)−⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩≤12∥y−x∥w2, with hidden wi>0, 0<μ≤1. A minimizer x⋆ exists with f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ, Δ≥0. Exact joint value–gradient calls target f(x^)−f(x⋆)≤ε, ε>0, deterministically. Only d,x0 are public; the setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

(2) Multidimensional backtracking, derived bound (Kunstner et al. 2023), Prop. 3.2, Thm. 5.3 O(1+dκℓ+dlog+⁡(L/α0)); twice differentiable; initial set contains an optimal preconditioner. (1): leading accuracy term saves dκ when ℓ≳d/κh4. Needs neither initial set nor twice differentiability. (1): warm-up dκh4 replaces dlog+⁡(L/α0); extra κ2 inside accuracy logarithm.
(3) OSGM-R (Gao et al. 2025), Thm. 6.2 O(1+κL2∥P1−P^∥F2+κℓ) on diagonal candidate matrices; known L,f⋆. (1): leading accuracy term saves κ when ℓ≳dh4/κ; no L,f⋆ knowledge or uncontrolled regret initialization. (1): dimension-dependent warm-up; extra κ2 inside logarithm. Covers diagonal metrics, whereas (3) also permits full matrices.
(4) Centre of gravity, derived bound (Bubeck 2015), Sec. 2.1 O(d+dlog⁡(1+Δκ4/ε)) including secant probes; known μ; exact centroid computation. (1): no μ knowledge. For d=ℓ=κ→∞, total O(κ3/2h4) versus O(κ2); gain requires d≫κ, ℓ≫κh4. (1): worse oracle cost when d≲κ or warm-up dominates.

Secant metric J satisfies J⪯diag(w)⪯J/μ. All costs count joint value–gradient calls. Updates in (1) use no w,μ,Δ,ε,f⋆; its budget depends on them and is not a stopping certificate.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.DiagonalSmoothStronglyConvexBlackBox

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  d : ℕ
  [nonzero : NeZero d]
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

attribute [instance] Public.nonzero

structure Params extends Public where
  w : Fin d → ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d) → ℝ
  Query p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  Reply p := ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  Output p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.μ ∧ q.μ ≤ 1 ∧ (∀ i, 0 < q.w i) ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f oracle :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ k seed x, oracle.answer k (0, x) seed = (f x, gradient f x)) ∧
    (∀ x y, f y ≤ f x + ⟪gradient f x, y - x⟫ + (∑ i, q.w i * (y i - x i) ^ 2) / 2) ∧
    (∀ x y, f x + ⟪gradient f x, y - x⟫ + q.μ * (∑ i, q.w i * (y i - x i) ^ 2) / 2 ≤ f y) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ f q.x0 - f xstar ≤ q.Δ)
  successful q f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.DiagonalSmoothStronglyConvexBlackBox
